newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares hit all-time high,up 40% this year.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares hit all-time high,up 40% this year.

text.p: Slovenian shares surged 2.44 percent to an all-time high on Wednesday, pushed up by strong demand for drug maker Lek and bank SKB.
The 11-share SBI index jumped 38.72 points to 1,622.4. Since the beginning of 1997 the SBI has risen 40.3 percent.
The previous all-time high was reached on June 28, 1994, when it closed at 1,598.02.
"I expect very vivacious movement in these two shares (Lek and SKB) over the short term -- the upward trend is most likely to continue," Davor Dubokovic, a trader at Eastbrokers said.
Dubokovic said the market may receive a further boost when pharmaceutical producer Krka is listed on Monday.
Turnover rose to 598.9 million tolars from 549 million.
Overall 11 shares rose, nine fell and one was unchanged, while four were untraded.
Bank SKB was the most active, firming 2.67 percent to 76,900 tolars on volume of 3,967 shares for total turnover of 307.4 million tolars.
"SKB's global depositary receipts are expected to be listed on the London bourse within the next 10 days, so SKB could continue to grow in the near future," one broker said.
Pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus was the biggest gainer, jumping 6.52 percent to 16,000 tolars on volume of 970 shares for total turnover of 14.7 million tolars.
Ordinary shares of Dolenjska bank led the day's decliners, falling 4.11 percent to 14,010 tolars on volume of 153 shares for total turnover of 2.2 million tolars.
Drug maker Lek jumped 4.28 percent to 31,700 tolars on volume of 6,494 shares for total turnover of 204.8 million tolars.
